V-CAPS: Virtual Cybersecurity AP Course Supplemental

Font Size: + -
Share & Bookmark Share & Bookmark, Press Enter to show all options, press Tab go to next option
Feedback Print

 

About the V-CAPS Challenge

The Virtual Cybersecurity AP Course Supplemental (V-CAPS) Challenge is a 12-week virtual learning experience designed for high school students enrolled in advanced placement (AP) or equivalent dual-credit computing courses to transform theory into demonstrated skills. Students will work in teams of five in a structured, real-world customer environment on a hosted Vulnerability Disclosure Program (VDP) platform that mirrors industry workflows. The project culminates with a team presentation to an audience of cybersecurity professionals. 

Apply Now | FAQ

 

Program Highlights

  • 80+ hours of hands-on cybersecurity experience through ethical hacking activities, industry instructors, and team-based projects
  • Work in a real-world cybersecurity environment modeled after professional vulnerability disclosure programs
  • Learn from active top-tier security researchers through weekly meetings, guidance, and feedback
  • Build practical skills in vulnerability assessment, penetration testing, and secure software development
  • Collaborate on a team of five students to research, identify and report security issues
  • Present your work to cybersecurity professionals during the program's final showcase
  • Explore cybersecurity career pathways and connect with industry experts

What You'll Earn

Students who successfully complete the challenge will receive:

  • Certificate of Completion recognizing successful participation and applied cybersecurity skills aligned with Penetration Tester and Vulnerability Assessment Analyst work roles
  • Real-world project experience that can be included on college, scholarship, and career applications
  • Professional skills in teamwork, communication, problem-solving, and ethical cybersecurity research
  • Stipend up to $1,725 for participants who meet attendance requirements and successfully complete all program milestones, including assignments, reflections, the final presentation, and post-program survey. See FAQ for further details.

2027 Schedule

Pre-Application Information Session (Optional) 

November 9, 2026 at 10-11am Pacific (1-2pm Eastern)

Learn about the program, meet program staff, ask questions about the application process.

Registration Link | Recording Link (when available)

Onboarding Orientation (Required for Accepted Applicants) 

December 29, 2026 at 1-2:30 pm Pacific (4-5:30 pm Eastern)

Form your team, set up program accounts and tools, review expectations, and prepare for the 12-week challenge. This required session ensures everyone is ready to get started and succeed in the program.

Weekly Meetings (Required for Accepted Applicants) 

January 12 to March 31, 2027 (12 weeks)

Cohort 1: Meets on Tuesdays, 4-6pm Eastern
Cohort 2: Meets on Wednesdays, 5-7pm Pacific

Each cohort will have 25 students divided into teams of five. 

  • Week 1 - Workshop begins: Tooling, expectations, and the ethics of security research.
  • Week 2 - Security Research overview, in-depth coverage of the OWASP Top 10. 
  • Week 3 - Introduction to AI as a tool and a target (core differentiation).
  • Week 4 - Finalize targets, vulnerability class, and refine methodology using custom tooling that incorporates AI.
  • Weeks 5 to 9 - Teams work independently during these weeks. Weekly meetings will cover vulnerability hunting and scoring. 
  • Weeks 10 to 12 - Wrap up final scoring and project presentation. Complete feedback survey.

Meet the Instructors

Top-tier active security researchers will facilitate the challenge.

 

Ads Dawson

Founding Offensive AI Research, Offensive Security | Security Researcher
Remote Threat

LinkedIn

 

 

Adam (Ads) Dawson is a security researcher and Founding AI Engineer at Remote Threat, an offensive AI security company. His experience includes red teaming AI systems for government and military organizations to find security weaknesses before adversaries do — a practice at the heart of what V-CAPS students will learn. Ranked #2 in the US on HackerOne, one of the world's largest ethical hacking platforms, Ads was selected by Bugcrowd as a top-tier researcher to co-instruct V-CAPS alongside his good friend NahamSec (Ben Sadeghipour) and Nathan A. Zaldivar.

Ads founded the OWASP GenAI Security Project, the leading open-source resource on AI security risks and the fastest project to reach flagship status in OWASP's history. He is the author of AI Native LLM Security (Packt, 2025) and has published five research papers on AI security evaluation. His policy work includes shaping the EU AI Act's Code of Practice as a contractor to the European AI Office.

In V-CAPS, Ads draws on 13+ years of cybersecurity experience to guide students through real-world vulnerability discovery on federal systems, teaching how AI can be used as both a security tool and a target for attacks.

 

Nathan Miranda (AKA rye)

Senior Ethical Hacker | Bug Bounty Hunter
Spectrum | Bugcrowd
LinkedIn

 

 

Nathan, better known as rye, is a Senior Ethical Hacker who has spent the last six years breaking things for a living. As a Penetration Tester, he lives in three lanes: web application security, LLM security, and security automation. If it's boring and repetitive, he’s probably already written a script for it.

For the last two years, he's brought that same energy to bug bounty — hunting real world vulnerabilities part time and turning what he finds into automation for everyone in the vulnerability remediation pipeline. Nathan holds CompTIA Security+ and the Burp Suite Certified Practitioner cert, and publishes his tooling, writeups, and experiments at rye.coffee.

In V-CAPS, rye brings the automator's mindset and has a passion in showing students how to find vulnerabilities faster, report them cleaner, and make remediation easier for all humans involved. His motive is to make things simpler for future hackers to do bad for good.


Ben Sadeghipour (AKA NahamSec)

Co-Founder/CEO | Cybersecurity Content Creator | Hacker/Security Researcher
LinkedIn

 

 

 

Ben Sadeghipour, known online as NahamSec, is an offensive security researcher, educator, and founder of HackingHub, an interactive browser-based platform for hands-on security training. With more than a decade of experience in offensive security, he has spent over 12 years as a bug bounty hunter on HackerOne, reporting hundreds of valid vulnerabilities to organizations worldwide. Before launching HackingHub, Ben spent six years at HackerOne, where he helped build its global hacker community, worked on the triage team, and helped create its live hacking events. He also runs NahamCon, a hacking conference for the security community. Through his NahamSec channels, Ben teaches security to an audience of more than 600,000 people across YouTube, X, and LinkedIn, and he speaks regularly at industry events on bug bounty, web application security, and careers in cybersecurity.

Ready to Apply?

Applications are submitted individually. Teams of five will be formed after participants are selected.

This program is designed for high school students who:

  • Are currently enrolled in an Advanced Placement (AP) or equivalent dual-credit course in cybersecurity, IT, computer science, or a related STEM course
  • Must be a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, or lawful permanent resident (green card holder)
  • Reside in the United States or a U.S. territory
  • Prerequisites: Teamwork readiness; comfort with ambiguity; and baseline technical skills: internet fundamentals, proxy usage, and OWASP Top 10:2025 concepts.

Materials Needed for the Application

  • Information about your cybersecurity, computer science, or related coursework and learning experiences.
  • Your current course schedule.
  • A brief description describing why you are interested in participating in the V-CAPS Challenge and what you can contribute to the program.
  • A brief description of your experience working on teams, your role, challenges, and lessons learned.
  • The required forms listed below.

The following Required Forms must be uploaded with your application. Click the link to download or print the form.

  1. V-CAPS Student Participation Agreement and Parent/Guardian Consent Form (Signed by all students. Also signed by parent/guardian if student under age 18.)
  2. Photo Release Form
    • Under age 18: signed by parent/guardian
    • Age 18 or older: signed by student
  3. Minor Security Researcher Agreement (required only for applicants under age 18; signed by both student and parent/guardian)
  4. An Instructor Endorsement Form from a teacher who can speak to your academic preparation, technical abilities, and readiness for the program, such as your AP or dual-credit teacher.

Incomplete applications will not be considered!

 

Timeline

  • Submit a completed application, including instructor endorsement and required forms by December 11, 2026 at 3:59 PM Pacific (6:59 PM Eastern). 
  • Applicants will be notified by email on approximately December 21, 2026.
